questions.stemHtml: In a dog blood pressure experiment, a researcher injected phentolamine first followed by epinephrine and the recordings of the effect are shown in the diagram given below. This phenomenon is known as?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Vasomotor reversal of Dale

 

  • Normally epinephrine produces a biphasic response on blood pressure which is characterized by increase in BP followed by decrease in BP. First increase is due to stimulation of alpha 1 receptors and later on decrease is due to stimulation of beta 2 receptors.
  • However, If alpha blockers like phentolamine are already given and then we administer epinephrine, it causes only exaggerated fall in blood pressure. This is called vasomotor reversal of Dale.
  • If we give same dose of a drug repeatedly and there is decrease in effect of the drug, it is called tachyphylaxis. It is shown by drugs like ephedrine.
  • There is no term like phentolamine epinephrine coupling.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is admitted to the intensive care unit for acute exacerbation of his respiratory symptoms. Cultures are taken, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa is isolated from his sputum sample. The healthcare team is considering various antibiotic options to target this specific bacterial strain. Which of the following antibiotics is not effective against infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Vancomycin

 

  • Among the antibiotics mentioned, Vancomycin is not effective against Pseudomonas infections.

  • Vancomycin is primarily used to treat Gram-positive bacterial infections, such as those caused by Staphylococcus aureus (including methicillin-resistant strains) and Enterococcus species.

  • Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is a common pathogen associated with Pseudomonas infections, is inherently resistant to Vancomycin.

  • The other antibiotics mentioned—Ceftazidime, Ciprofloxacin, and Rifampicin—are known to have activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and can be used to treat infections caused by this bacterium.

questions.stem: Adrenaline acting via beta 2 receptors causes bronchodilation whereas histamine acting through H1 receptors cause bronchoconstriction. Which type of antagonism it is?
questions.solutionHtml:
strong>Ans. D. Physiological Antagonism

 

Explanation of Options:

 

A) Pharmacological Antagonism: This term generally refers to one drug reducing the effectiveness of another drug, typically through receptor competition or a similar mechanism at the molecular level. Since adrenaline and histamine act on different receptors to produce opposite physiological effects, this option is not correct.

 

B) Chemical Antagonism: This occurs when one drug directly reacts with another to neutralize its effects e.g. antacids neutralize gastric acid and protamine neutralize heparin. There is no direct chemical reaction between adrenaline and histamine, making this option incorrect.

 

C) Physical Antagonism: This would imply that the drugs physically interfere with each other e.g. charcoal adbsorbs many drugs and is used in drug poisoning.

 

D) Physiological Antagonism: This is the correct answer. Physiological antagonism occurs when two drugs produce opposite effects in the same physiological system. Adrenaline causes bronchodilation via beta-2 receptors, while histamine causes bronchoconstriction via H1 receptors. These drugs act on different receptor types but have opposite effects on the same physiological system, namely the bronchial smooth muscle.

questions.stem: A farmer presents to the emergency department with pinpoint pupil, diarrhea, sweating, excessive lacrimation, salivation and garlic dour. on examination there is bradycardia and BP is 80/60 mm Hg pulse rate is 56/min and his plasma cholinesterase level was 52 U/mL. Which of the following is antidote for treatment of this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
pan>

 

Explanation of Options:

 

A) Pralidoxine: This drug is typically used alongside atropine for treating organophosphate poisoning to reactivate acetylcholinesterase, but it does not counteract the cholinergic symptoms the patient is experiencing.

 

B) Atropine: This is the correct answer. The farmer's symptoms such as pinpoint pupils, excessive salivation, and bradycardia suggest cholinergic toxicity, likely from organophosphate exposure. Atropine acts as an antagonist at muscarinic cholinergic receptors and would counteract many of the symptoms observed.

 

C) Physostigmine: This drug is a cholinesterase inhibitor and would worsen the symptoms of cholinergic toxicity, making it an inappropriate treatment in this case.

 

D) N-acetylcysteine: This is commonly used for acetaminophen overdose and would not be effective for treating symptoms of cholinergic toxicity.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is scheduled to receive a new medication. The physician explains the mechanism of action and potential side effects of finasteride to the patient and his family. Which of the following is true about finasteride?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases the production of testosterone.

options.label: B
options.text: It act as an antagonist of androgen receptors.

options.label: C
options.text: It can cause sexual side effects such as decreased libido and erectile dysfunction.

options.label: D
options.text: It is only effective in reducing symptoms of BPH in the short-term.

questions.answerText: It can cause sexual side effects such as decreased libido and erectile dysfunction.
questions.solutionHtml:
>

Explanation:

  • Finasteride like drugs are a class of medications used to treat BPH by reducing the size of the prostate gland.
  • They work by inhibiting the enzyme 5 alpha reductase, which converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT).
  • By reducing the levels of DHT, 5 alpha reductase inhibitors can shrink the prostate gland and improve urinary symptoms associated with BPH.
  • A potential side effect of these medications is sexual dysfunction, including decreased libido and erectile dysfunction.
  • These medications can take several months to achieve their maximum effect and can provide long-term relief of BPH symptoms.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old researcher is studying a novel antiviral drug that has shown promise in in-vitro studies. The researcher is in the process of planning the clinical development of the drug. She explains to her team that the next step involves a phase zero clinical trial, which will be crucial in determining whether to move on to phase I trials. The team is confused, as they are not familiar with phase zero clinical trials. Which of the following statements is true regarding phase zero clinical trials, that would help the team understand its significance?

options.label: A
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials are typically conducted in animal models to assess the safety and efficacy of a new drug.

options.label: B
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials are comprehensive studies designed to provide conclusive data on the safety and efficacy of a new drug.

options.label: C
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials primarily focus on pharmacokinetics, particularly on the movement of the drug in the human body.

options.label: D
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials are also known as therapeutic trials and aim to cure or mitigate symptoms of the disease in question.

questions.answerText: Phase zero clinical trials primarily focus on pharmacokinetics, particularly on the movement of the drug in the human body.
questions.solutionHtml:
Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Phase zero clinical trials are typically conducted in animal models to assess the safety and efficacy of a new drug: This statement is incorrect. Phase zero clinical trials are human trials that precede phase I trials. They are not animal studies.

 

B) Phase zero clinical trials are comprehensive studies designed to provide conclusive data on the safety and efficacy of a new drug: This is incorrect. Phase zero trials are not designed to provide comprehensive data on safety and efficacy but are focused on pharmacokinetics and perhaps some initial pharmacodynamic data.

 

C) Phase zero clinical trials primarily focus on pharmacokinetics, particularly on the movement of the drug in the human body: This is correct. The main aim of phase zero trials is to gather preliminary data on pharmacokinetics and assess whether the drug behaves in humans as it does in preclinical models.

 

D) Phase zero clinical trials are also known as therapeutic trials and aim to cure or mitigate symptoms of the disease in question: This is incorrect. Phase zero trials are exploratory trials that precede phase I trials; they are not focused on therapeutic outcomes.

 

Therefore, the statement that would best help the team understand the significance of phase zero trials is that they primarily focus on pharmacokinetics and provide initial human data on the movement and metabolism of the drug.



ore, the statement that would best help the team understand the significance of phase zero trials is that they primarily focus on pharmacokinetics and provide initial human data on the movement and metabolism of the drug.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease presents to the emergency department with complaints of muscle weakness, nausea, and abdominal cramping. Laboratory testing shows that the patient has hyperkalemia, with a serum potassium level of 6.5 mEq/L. The patient's medications are reviewed, and it is discovered that he has been taking several drugs for his cardiac conditions and hypertension. Upon further evaluation, it is determined that one of these drugs may be contributing to the patient's hyperkalemia. Which of the following drugs should be stopped in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Enalapril

  • Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor used in the treatment of hypertension and can cause hyperkalemia as a side effect.
  • Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic and Furosemide is a loop diuretic, these can cause hypokalemia but not hyperkalemia.
  • Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker that does not typically cause electrolyte imbalances.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) consults his physician for treatment options. The physician recommends the use of rabeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor. Which of the following statements about proton pump inhibitors is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Proton pump inhibitors are available as enteric-coated tablets.

options.label: B
options.text: Proton pump inhibitors act from the luminal side of gastric parietal cells.

options.label: C
options.text: Proton pump inhibitors are inactive at neutral pH.

options.label: D
options.text: Proton pump inhibitors should be taken half an hour before food

questions.answerText: Proton pump inhibitors act from the luminal side of gastric parietal cells.
questions.solutionHtml:
Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Proton pump inhibitors are available as enteric-coated tablets: This statement is TRUE. The enteric coating allows the medication to pass through the stomach without being destroyed by the stomach acid, eventually dissolving in the intestine for absorption.

 

B) Proton pump inhibitors act from the luminal side of gastric parietal cells: This statement is FALSE. Proton pump inhibitors, including rabeprazole, act from the acidic canaliculus inside the gastric parietal cell, not from the luminal side.

 

C) Proton pump inhibitors are inactive at neutral pH: This statement is TRUE. Proton pump inhibitors are prodrugs that are activated in an acidic environment, which allows them to act specifically on the stomach's acid-secreting cells.

 

D) Proton pump inhibitors should be taken half an hour before food: This statement is TRUE. Taking proton pump inhibitors around 30 minutes before eating ensures better activation of the drug, as the stomach starts producing acid in response to eating, thereby optimizing the drug's efficacy.

 

Therefore, the statement that is INCORRECT regarding proton pump inhibitors is that they act from the luminal side of gastric parietal cells.



ore, the statement that is INCORRECT regarding proton pump inhibitors is that they act from the luminal side of gastric parietal cells.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male presents with symptoms of urinary urgency, frequency, and nocturia. He has been diagnosed with overactive bladder and his previous medication (oxybutynin) was not effective in managing his symptoms. Which of the following drugs is a beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist that may be effective in treating this patient's symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Calibri,sans-serif">Ans. C. Vibegron

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Tolterodine: This drug is an antimuscarinic agent, not a beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist. It is commonly used in the treatment of overactive bladder but works through a different mechanism of action than beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonists.

 

B) Memantine: Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist used primarily in the treatment of moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease. It has no role in the treatment of overactive bladder.

 

C) Vibegron: This is a beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist (similar to mirabegron) that is used in the treatment of overactive bladder. By stimulating beta-3 adrenergic receptors in the detrusor muscle of the bladder, it relaxes the muscle and improves symptoms like urinary urgency and frequency.

 

D) Levetiracetam: Levetiracetam is an antiepileptic drug that is used to treat various types of seizures. It has no role in the treatment of overactive bladder.

questions.stem: A patient is admitted to the emergency department for treatment of a drug overdose. The identity of the drug is unknown, but it is observed that when the urine pH is acidic, the renal clearance of the drug is less than GFR and that when the urine pH is alkaline, the clearance is greater than GFR. The drug probably is?
questions.solutionHtml:
The drug is most likely a weak acid (Choice B).

 

Explanation:

 

When the urine pH is acidic, the renal clearance of a weak acid drug is less than the glomerular filtration rate (GFR). This is because in acidic urine, weak acid drugs remain predominantly in their non-ionized form, which hinders their excretion into the urine. As a result, their renal clearance is limited.

 

On the other hand, when the urine pH is alkaline, the renal clearance of a weak acid drug is greater than the GFR. In alkaline urine, weak acid drugs become ionized, which promotes their excretion into the urine. This leads to a higher renal clearance compared to the GFR.

 

Strong acids (Choice A) and strong bases (Choice D) are usually fully ionized and do not undergo significant changes in their excretion based on urine pH.

 

Therefore, based on the observed changes in renal clearance in response to urine pH, the drug in question is most likely a weak acid (Choice B).



ore, based on the observed changes in renal clearance in response to urine pH, the drug in question is most likely a weak acid (Choice B).

questions.stem: A 43-year-old, insulin-dependent diabetic patient is diagnosed with hypertension and begins therapy with an antihypertensive agent. Three days later, he measures his blood glucose at home and finds that it is 53 mg/dL. He recalibrates his glucose testing apparatus and repeats the test, only to find that the first reading was accurate. He is concerned that his hypoglycemia did not produce the normal premonitory signs and symptoms. Which of the following medications was most likely prescribed to treat his hypertension?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Propranolol

  • Propranolol belongs to the class of medications known as beta-blockers. Beta-blockers can mask the typical signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia, such as tachycardia, palpitations and tremors by blocking the beta-adrenergic receptors that are responsible for these responses. As a result, the patient may experience hypoglycemia without being aware of it.
  • In contrast, medications like captopril (A), diltiazem (B), and methyldopa (C) are not known to mask the signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia.
  • Note that beta blockers do not stop sweating as it is mediated by M3 muscarinic receptors.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is WRONG about amiodarone?

options.label: A
options.text: It is the longest acting anti arrhythmic drug.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans B. It has positive ionotropic action.

  • Amiodarone is a potent antiarrhythmic medication with multiple actions on cardiac ion channels. However, it does not have a positive ionotropic action. In fact, amiodarone has predominantly negative inotropic effects, meaning it reduces the force of cardiac contractions.
  • The correct statements about amiodarone are:
    • It is the longest-acting antiarrhythmic drug: Amiodarone has a half-life of around 3 weeks, meaning it remains in the body for an extended period. This allows for a once-daily dosing regimen in many cases.
    • It contains iodine: Amiodarone contains around 40 percent iodine, which contribute to its structure. This iodine content is responsible for some of the medication's potential adverse effects, such as thyroid abnormalities.
    • It can cause pulmonary fibrosis: Amiodarone has been associated with pulmonary toxicity, which can manifest as lung inflammation and fibrosis.

questions.stem: Metformin is least likely to reduce blood sugar in which of the following patients?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Non-diabetics

 

  • Metformin is an oral medication commonly used to treat type 2 diabetes. It works by reducing glucose production in the liver, improving insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues, and reducing glucose absorption in the intestines. As a result, metformin helps to lower blood sugar levels in individuals with diabetes.
  • In non-diabetic individuals, who already have normal blood sugar regulation, the use of metformin is not indicated. Metformin does not cause hypoglycemia and since the blood sugar levels of non-diabetics are within the normal range, metformin cannot further reduce blood sugar.
  • The other options listed are more likely to benefit from metformin in terms of blood sugar reduction:

 

A. Obese diabetics: Metformin is commonly prescribed to obese individuals with type 2 diabetes as it helps improve insulin sensitivity and control blood sugar levels.

 

C. Type 2 diabetics: Metformin is considered a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes and is widely used to reduce blood sugar levels in these patients.

 

D. Diabetics not responding to sulfonylureas: When individuals with diabetes do not respond adequately to sulfonylureas (another class of antidiabetic medication), metformin is often added as an adjunct therapy to help improve blood sugar control.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman goes to her dermatologist to have a mole removed. The patient tells her physician that she had an allergic reaction to a local anesthetic the last time she had dental work performed. Examination of her dental records by her dentist reveals that the patient received chlorprocaine for a tooth extraction. Which of the following drugs would be appropriate for the present procedure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Lignocaine

 

The patient had a reaction to chlorprocaine, a type of ester local anaesthetic. An allergy to one type of ester local anaesthetic could potentially mean that she may react to other types of ester local anaesthetics, since they have similar structures and are metabolized in a similar way. Benzocaine, procaine and cocaine are all ester local anaesthetics, so should be avoided in this patient. It would be safest to use an amide local anaesthetic in this patient. The only amide anaesthetic in the choices is lignocaine.

questions.stem: Following the treatment of an oral abscess with clindamycin, a patient develops a greenish, foul-smelling watery diarrhea with left lower quadrant pain. Other signs and symptoms include fever, leukocytosis, and lethargy. If the toxin produced by Clostridium difficile is detected in the stool, the patient would most appropriately be treated with:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Fidaxomicin.

 

  • Based on the scenario provided, the patient likely has pseudomembranous colitis, a common side effect of antibiotic treatment, particularly with broad-spectrum antibiotics like clindamycin. The symptoms described in the question: greenish, foul-smelling watery diarrhea, left lower quadrant pain, fever, leukocytosis, and lethargy – are consistent with this diagnosis and presence of toxin of Clostridium difficile in the stool confirms the diagnosis of pseudomembranous colitis.
  • Pseudomembranous colitis, also known as Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) is a common cause of antibiotic-associated diarrhea, and one of the primary treatments for CDI is antibiotics that specifically target the infection. Fidaxomicin is a narrow-spectrum antibiotic that is effective against Clostridium difficile and is now the drug of choice for treatment of pseudomembranous colitis.
  • The other options listed are:
  • Vancomycin is another antibiotic that is commonly used to treat CDI. However, vancomycin is no longer drug of choice for pseudomembranous colitis. Further, whenever used, vancomycin is preferred by oral route for treatment of this condition than by intravenous route.
  • Loperamide is an antidiarrheal medication that helps to relieve diarrhea symptoms by slowing down the movement of the intestines. However, it does not treat the underlying infection and would not be appropriate as the sole treatment for this patient.
  • Metronidazole is an antibiotic that has been used in the past as a first-line treatment for CDI. However, due to increasing resistance rates, current guidelines recommend reserving metronidazole for mild cases or as an alternative treatment option.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old female presents to the clinic with a palpable lump in her left breast that she noticed while showering. She reports no associated pain, discharge, or skin changes. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known family history of breast or ovarian cancer. Her last mammogram was two years ago and showed no abnormalities. After appropriate investigations including mammogram, ultrasound, and biopsy, she is diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. The biopsy reveals that the cancer is HER2-positive, but estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) negative. Which of the following drugs, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, would be suitable for treating this patient's breast cancer?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Lapatinib.

  • Lapatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that is commonly used in the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer. In this case, the patient has been diagnosed with stage II breast cancer that is HER2-positive but estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) negative. Lapatinib is effective in targeting the HER2 receptor, which is overexpressed in HER2-positive breast cancer cells. Other tyrosine kinase inhibitor used for breast cancer is neratinib.
  • Sorafenib (Option A) is primarily used in the treatment of renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma.
  • Imatinib (Option B) is drug of choice for the treatment of CML and GIST.
  • Pazopanib (Option C) is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma and soft tissue sarcoma.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old female patient is undergoing chemotherapy for breast cancer. The oncology team is concerned about the risk of febrile neutropenia due to the chemotherapeutic regimen. They are contemplating the use of a granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) and discuss the option of using pegylated-filgrastim. Which of the following is true about pegylated-filgrastim?

options.label: A
options.text: Duration of action is longer than filgrastim

options.label: B
options.text: Added advantage is that it can be taken orally

options.label: D
options.text: It is not effective in the treatment of severe neutropenia.

questions.answerText: Duration of action is longer than filgrastim
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Duration of action is longer than filgrastim.

 

Pegylated-filgrastim, also known as peg-filgrastim, is a long-acting formulation of filgrastim that is used to stimulate the production of white blood cells in patients receiving chemotherapy. The addition of polyethylene glycol (PEG) to filgrastim increases its molecular weight and slows down its clearance from the body, resulting in a longer duration of action compared to normal filgrastim.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Added advantage is that it can be taken orally: Pegylated-filgrastim is administered subcutaneously and is not available in oral form.

 

Option C. It requires renal dose adjustment: Pegylated-filgrastim does not usually require renal dose adjustment, making this statement incorrect.

 

Option D. It is not effective in the treatment of severe neutropenia: Pegylated-filgrastim is effective in the treatment of neutropenia and is often used to reduce the risk of infection in patients undergoing chemotherapy.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man is experiencing recurrent urinary tract infections. His healthcare team is considering various antibiotics, including fluoroquinolones, for his treatment. Which of the following fluoroquinolones is not typically effective for treating urinary tract infections?
questions.solutionHtml:
lign:justify;">P: Pefloxacin

  • M: Moxifloxacin

  • T: Trovafloxacin
     

    • Explanation of all the options:

     

    A) Ofloxacin: This fluoroquinolone is commonly used for treating urinary tract infections and is generally effective against a wide range of bacteria that can cause UTIs.

     

    B) Levofloxacin: This is another fluoroquinolone antibiotic frequently used in the treatment of UTIs and is generally effective for this purpose.

     

    C) Moxifloxacin: This is the correct answer. Moxifloxacin is generally not recommended for treating UTIs. It has reduced effectiveness against the typical bacteria that cause UTIs as compared to other fluoroquinolones.

     

    D) Lomefloxacin: Like ofloxacin and levofloxacin, lomefloxacin is generally effective for treating UTIs.

     

    Therefore, among the given options, Moxifloxacin is typically not effective for treating urinary tract infections.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Thyroxine

 

Thyroxine acts via nuclear receptors whereas all other drugs mentioned in the options act via G protein coupled receptors.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male patient with a history of chronic pain is being managed on an oral pain medication. The healthcare team is monitoring the patient's response to medication and decides to take periodic plasma concentration samples. The team wants to evaluate the rate at which the drug is absorbed into the patient's system. Which of the following parameters on a plasma concentration vs. time graph would be most indicative of the rate of drug absorption for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
2.0pt;">Ans. D. Tmax

 

Explanation of Options:

 

A) Area under the Curve (AUC): This parameter reflects the total drug exposure over time but does not give insights into the rate of drug absorption.

 

B) Half-life (T1/2): This measures how long it takes for the drug concentration to decrease to half its initial value, more related to the elimination phase rather than the absorption rate.

 

C) Maximum concentration (Cmax): This indicates the peak concentration of the drug in the bloodstream but doesn't specify how quickly this level is reached.

 

D) Time to reach maximum concentration (Tmax): This is the time it takes for the drug to reach its peak concentration in the plasma. It gives an indication of how quickly the drug is absorbed into the system.

 

Therefore, the time to reach maximum concentration (Tmax) is the best parameter to evaluate the rate of drug absorption.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Non-competitive.

 

The above given graph is showing non-competitive inhibition.

 

When the substrate and the inhibitor are chemically not similar and have different shapes, the inhibitor binds away from the active site, i.e., at the allosteric site. This type of inhibition is known as non-competitive inhibition.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old male patient with chronic gout is under consideration for a change in treatment plan due to poor response to conventional therapies like allopurinol and colchicine. The healthcare team is discussing the potential use of rasburicase. What is the mechanism of action of rasburicase?

options.label: B
options.text: Conversion of uric acid to allantoin

questions.answerText: Conversion of uric acid to allantoin
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Conversion of uric acid to allantoin.

 

Option A. Inhibition of xanthine oxidase: This is the mechanism of action for allopurinol, not pegloticase. Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, which is an enzyme involved in the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid.

 

Option B. Conversion of uric acid to allantoin: Rasburicase is a recombinant uricase enzyme that converts uric acid into allantoin, which is more soluble and easier to excrete through the kidneys. This action helps to lower high levels of uric acid in patients with chronic gout.

 

Option C. Increase excretion of uric acid: Some medications like probenecid work by this mechanism to increase the renal excretion of uric acid.

 

Option D. Inhibition of granulocyte migration: Colchicine works through inhibiting granulocyte migration, but pegloticase primarily works by metabolizing uric acid.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman has been diagnosed with stage IV melanoma and is scheduled to receive immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. The physician explains the mechanism of action and potential side effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors to the patient and her family. Which of the following is true about immune checkpoint inhibitors?

options.label: A
options.text: Nivolumab works by blocking the PD-1 receptor and is used to treat various types of cancer.

options.label: B
options.text: Bevacizumab works by inhibiting angiogenesis and is used to treat solid tumors.

options.label: C
options.text: Rituximab works by depleting B cells and is used to treat lymphoma and autoimmune disorders.

options.label: D
options.text: Trastuzumab works by targeting the HER2 receptor and is used to treat breast cancer.

questions.answerText: Nivolumab works by blocking the PD-1 receptor and is used to treat various types of cancer.
questions.solutionHtml:
f cancer.

 

Explanation:

 

Among the given options, only nivolumab is an immune check point inhibitor whereas other drugs mentioned in the options act by other mechanisms.

  • Immune checkpoint inhibitors are a type of immunotherapy that work by releasing the brakes on the immune system, allowing it to attack cancer cells more effectively. Nivolumab is a monoclonal antibody that blocks the PD-1 receptor on T cells, which prevents the inhibition of T cell activation and enhances the immune system's ability to attack cancer cells. Nivolumab has been approved for the treatment of various types of cancer, including Hodgkin’s lymphoma,  melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and kidney cancer.
  • Bevacizumab is a monoclonal antibody against VEGF that inhibits angiogenesis, the formation of new blood vessels, and is used to treat solid tumors.
  • Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody against CD20 that depletes B cells and is used to treat lymphoma and autoimmune disorders.
  • Trastuzumab is a monoclonal antibody that targets the HER2 receptor and is used to treat breast cancer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a correct match with respect to the mechanism of action and clinical use of the given drugs?

options.label: A
options.text: Zavegepant - CGRP receptor antagonist used for the treatment of acute migraine attacks

options.label: B
options.text: Pembrolizumab – Immune check point inhibitor used for endometrial carcinoma

options.label: C
options.text: Ertugliflozin – SGLT2 inhibitor for treatment of diabetes mellitus

options.label: D
options.text: Ivabradine – Funny current blocker for treatment of decreased visual acuity

questions.answerText: Ivabradine – Funny current blocker for treatment of decreased visual acuity
questions.solutionHtml:
r treatment of decreased visual acuity.

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Zavegepant - CGRP receptor antagonist used for the treatment of acute migraine attacks: This is a correct match. Zavegepant is a calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist. It is used for the treatment of acute migraine attacks. CGRP is a neuropeptide that plays a role in the pathophysiology of migraines, and antagonists like Zavegepant block its activity, thereby alleviating symptoms.

 

B) Pembrolizumab – Immune check point inhibitor used for endometrial carcinoma: This is also a correct match. Pembrolizumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor that targets the PD-1 receptor. It is used for a variety of cancers, including endometrial carcinoma, especially in cases that are MSI-H or dMMR (microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair deficient).

 

C) Ertugliflozin – SGLT2 inhibitor for treatment of diabetes mellitus: This is another correct match. Ertugliflozin is a Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, which is used to manage blood sugar levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus. It works by inhibiting the reabsorption of glucose in the kidneys, thereby leading to the excretion of glucose in the urine.

 

D) Ivabradine – Funny current blocker for treatment of decreased visual acuity: This is the incorrect match. Ivabradine is indeed a "funny" current (If) blocker, but it is used for the treatment of certain types of chronic heart failure and angina pectoris (chest pain), not for treating decreased visual acuity.

 

Therefore, option D is not a correct match concerning the mechanism of action and clinical use of the given drug.



ore, option D is not a correct match concerning the mechanism of action and clinical use of the given drug.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old male presents to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. An electrocardiogram (ECG) reveals ST-segment elevation. The patient is diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and undergoes percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The cardiologist orders the patient to take an antiplatelet drug after the procedure to prevent further clot formation. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of clopidogrel, a commonly used antiplatelet drug?

options.label: A
options.text: Inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and decreases production of thromboxane A2, thereby reducing platelet activation and aggregation.

options.label: B
options.text: Blocks the P2Y12 receptor on platelets, inhibiting the activation and aggregation of platelets.

options.label: C
options.text: Inhibits the formation of fibrin by blocking the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin.

options.label: D
options.text: Binds to glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptors on the surface of activated platelets, preventing the aggregation of platelets.

questions.answerText: Blocks the P2Y12 receptor on platelets, inhibiting the activation and aggregation of platelets.
questions.solutionHtml:
strong>

 

Explanation:

 

  • Option B describes the mechanism of action of P2Y12 receptor inhibitors, such as clopidogrel, prasugrel, and ticagrelor. These drugs inhibit the activation and aggregation of platelets by blocking the P2Y12 receptor on the platelet surface.
  • Option A: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1), which is responsible for the production of thromboxane A2, a potent platelet activator and aggregator. By decreasing the production of thromboxane A2, aspirin reduces the activation and aggregation of platelets, thereby preventing further clot formation. Aspirin is commonly used as an antiplatelet drug for the prevention of cardiovascular events, such as myocardial infarction and stroke.
  • Option C describes the mechanism of action of anticoagulants, such as heparin and warfarin. These drugs inhibit the formation of fibrin by blocking the coagulation cascade and the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin.
  • Option D describes the mechanism of action of glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitors, such as abciximab, eptifibatide, and tirofiban. These drugs bind to glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptors on the surface of activated platelets, preventing the aggregation of platelets.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old female with a history of breast cancer presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up. She has recently completed a course of chemotherapy that included doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, and paclitaxel. Shortly after her chemotherapy, she developed febrile neutropenia and was treated with filgrastim and cefepime. She also has a history of hypertension controlled with amlodipine. She now reports experiencing symptoms of shortness of breath, fatigue, and palpitations. An echocardiogram reveals her ejection fraction has decreased to 40%. What is the most likely drug-related cause of her reduced ejection fraction?
questions.solutionHtml:
bri,sans-serif">Ans. B. Doxorubicin

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Filgrastim: This drug is used to stimulate the production of neutrophils and is commonly used to treat febrile neutropenia. It is not generally associated with cardiomyopathy or a reduced ejection fraction.

 

B) Doxorubicin: Doxorubicin is a chemotherapy agent known for its cardiotoxic effects, which can result in reduced ejection fraction and symptoms like shortness of breath, fatigue, and palpitations. Given the patient's recent chemotherapy regimen that included doxorubicin, this is the most likely cause of her decreased ejection fraction.

 

C) Cefepime: This antibiotic is commonly used to treat bacterial infections, including those that may occur with febrile neutropenia. It is not typically associated with reduced ejection fraction or cardiomyopathy.

 

D) Amlodipine: This drug is a calcium channel blocker used to treat hypertension. While it has cardiovascular effects, it is not generally associated with a reduced ejection fraction or cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding varenicline is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Varenicline is a nicotine replacement therapy that delivers nicotine through a transdermal patch

options.label: B
options.text: Varenicline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor that is used to treat depression

options.label: C
options.text: Varenicline is a partial agonist of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor that is used to aid smoking cessation

options.label: D
options.text: Varenicline is a long-acting beta2-agonist that is used to treat asthma

questions.answerText: Varenicline is a partial agonist of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor that is used to aid smoking cessation
questions.solutionHtml:
nbsp;

Explanation:

 

  • Varenicline is a medication that is used to aid smoking cessation. It is a partial agonist of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor, which means that it binds to the receptor and activates it to a lesser extent than nicotine. This reduces the pleasurable effects of smoking and decreases nicotine cravings.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Varenicline is a nicotine replacement therapy that delivers nicotine through a transdermal patch: this is incorrect because varenicline is not a nicotine replacement therapy that delivers nicotine through a transdermal patch. Nicotine replacement therapies include nicotine gum, lozenges, patches, and inhalers.

 

Option B. Varenicline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor that is used to treat depression: this is incorrect because varenicline is not a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). SSRIs are a class of medications that are primarily used to treat depression and anxiety disorders.

 

Option D. Varenicline is a long-acting beta2-agonist that is used to treat asthma: this is incorrect because varenicline is not a long-acting beta2-agonist (LABA). LABAs are a class of medications that are used to treat asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man who received a kidney transplant three months ago is admitted to the hospital with high-grade fever, malaise, and abdominal discomfort. On examination, he exhibits right upper quadrant tenderness. Lab investigations reveal abnormal liver enzymes, and a blood culture returns positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV). His current immunosuppressive regimen includes tacrolimus. What is the primary pharmacological action of tacrolimus that might have predisposed this patient to develop a CMV infection?
questions.solutionHtml:
nt-size:12.0pt">Ans. A. Inhibition of calcineurin

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Inhibition of calcineurin: Tacrolimus acts by inhibiting calcineurin, which plays a pivotal role in T-cell activation. This immunosuppressive action can make the patient susceptible to infections such as CMV.

 

B) Blockade of IL-2 receptor: This is a mechanism of other immunosuppressive drugs like basiliximab but not tacrolimus. Therefore, it is not relevant to the patient's current condition.

 

C) IMP dehydrogenase inhibition: This is the mechanism of mycophenolate mofetil, another immunosuppressive drug. It is not applicable to tacrolimus.

 

D) Dihydro-orotate dehydrogenase inhibition: This mechanism is associated with drugs like leflunomide but is not relevant to the action of tacrolimus.

 

Thus, the primary pharmacological action of tacrolimus that might have predisposed this patient to develop a CMV infection is the inhibition of calcineurin.



ore, it is not relevant to the patient's current condition.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old female with a history of glaucoma presents to the ophthalmologist with complaints of blurred vision and eye irritation. The patient reports that she has been using an anti-glaucoma medication for the past six months, and her symptoms began to appear gradually over the past few weeks. Upon further evaluation, it is discovered that the patient has experienced darkening of the iris and eyelid skin as well as increased length, thickness, and pigmentation of the eyelashes. Which of the following anti-glaucoma drugs is likely to produce these adverse effects?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Latanoprost.

  • The patient's symptoms are consistent with the known side effects of latanoprost, which is a prostaglandin analog used in the treatment of glaucoma.
  • Latanoprost can cause:
    • Pigmentation of Iris: It is also known as heterochromia iridis
    • Growth of Eyelashes: It is also called hypertrichosis
    • Macular Edema
    • Worsening of inflammation: So contraindicated in patients with uveitis.

questions.stem: A 78-year-old woman is taken to a neurologist by her family members. After thorough evaluation, the neurologist suggests the possibility of starting Aducanumab therapy, and the patient's family starts researching the medication. Which of the following statements about Aducanumab is FALSE?

options.label: B
options.text: Aducanumab works by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase to increase cholinergic transmission.

options.label: C
options.text: Aducanumab has received FDA approval for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

options.label: D
options.text: Aducanumab targets amyloid-beta plaques in the brain.

questions.answerText: Aducanumab works by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase to increase cholinergic transmission.
questions.solutionHtml:
-size:11pt">Another drug used for same purpose and acting by same mechanism is lecanemab

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Aducanumab is a monoclonal antibody: This statement is TRUE. Aducanumab is a monoclonal antibody designed to treat Alzheimer's disease by targeting amyloid-beta plaques in the brain.

 

B) Aducanumab works by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase to increase cholinergic transmission: This statement is FALSE. Aducanumab does not work by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase. Its primary mechanism is to target and remove amyloid-beta plaques.

 

C) Aducanumab has received FDA approval for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease: This statement is TRUE. Although its approval has been met with some controversy and debate, Aducanumab has been conditionally approved by the FDA for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

 

D) Aducanumab targets amyloid-beta plaques in the brain: This statement is TRUE. The drug is designed to bind to amyloid-beta plaques, thereby aiding in their removal and potentially slowing the progression of Alzheimer's disease, although definitive evidence for clinical benefit is still being evaluated.

 

Thus, the statement that is FALSE about Aducanumab is that it works by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase to increase cholinergic transmission.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is on theophylline therapy. He presents to the emergency department with symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and tremors. On examination, he has a heart rate of 110 beats per minute and a serum theophylline level of 30 mg/L (normal range 5-15 mg/L). Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for the patient's symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
omycin

 

Explanation:

 

  • Clarithromycin can interact with theophylline by inhibiting its metabolism, leading to an increase in serum concentration and an increased risk of toxicity.
  • Symptoms of theophylline toxicity include nausea, vomiting, tremors, seizures, and tachycardia. In severe cases, theophylline toxicity can lead to cardiac arrhythmias and seizures.
  • Other drugs that can interact with theophylline include ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, and fluvoxamine.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old patient with no significant medical history presents to the emergency department with a fever of 102°F and altered sensorium. Upon examination, you notice a petechial rash on the patient's arms and legs. You suspect meningococcal septicemia. Which of the following antibiotics is recommended as the first-line empiric therapy?
questions.solutionHtml:
n style="color:black">Ans. A. Ceftriaxone

 

Explanation:

  • Meningococcal septicemia is a medical emergency that requires prompt antibiotic therapy.
  • Empiric therapy with intravenous ceftriaxone is recommended as the first-line treatment for suspected meningococcal septicemia.
  • Penicillin G is an alternative option but is less commonly used due to increasing resistance.
  • Piperacillin-tazobactam and cotrimoxazole are not recommended as first-line treatments for meningococcal septicemia.
  • Definitive therapy should be based on culture and susceptibility results.

questions.stemHtml: What does IP in the figure shown stands for:

options.label: A
options.text: Drug is an instant release preparation

options.label: C
options.text: The standards according to Indian Pharmacopoeia

options.label: D
options.text: Drug tested preclinically via Intraperitoneal route

questions.answerText: The standards according to Indian Pharmacopoeia
questions.solutionHtml:
Pharmacopoeia

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

a. Drug is an instant release preparation: The term "IP" on a drug strip doesn't typically signify that the drug is an instant release preparation. This would usually be denoted by terms like "IR" rather than "IP."

 

b. Meant for intra pulmonary use: The abbreviation "IP" is not commonly used to denote that a drug is meant for intrapulmonary use. Instead, you would likely see terms such as "inhaler" or "nebulizer" or specific abbreviations for pulmonary administration.

 

c. The standards according to Indian Pharmacopoeia: This is the correct answer. The term "IP" is often used on pharmaceutical packaging in India to denote that the drug meets the standards laid out in the Indian Pharmacopoeia.

 

d. Drug tested preclinically via IntraPeritoneal route: "IP" is commonly used as an abbreviation for intraperitoneal in scientific research, but it is unlikely to be used in this context on a drug strip meant for patient use.

 

Therefore, the correct interpretation of "IP" on the drug strip of asthalin is that the drug complies with the standards of the Indian Pharmacopoeia.



ore, the correct interpretation of "IP" on the drug strip of asthalin is that the drug complies with the standards of the Indian Pharmacopoeia.

questions.stemHtml: A new antiarrhythmic drug is found to be effective against both atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. Its effect on action potential is shown in the Figure. The effect of this new drug is most similar to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Procainamide

  • This drug is decreasing the slope of phase 0 (Na+ channel blocking property) as well as increasing the action potential duration (K+ channel blocking property). Thus, it exhibits the properties of class Ia anti-arrhythmic agents.

  • Class Ia anti-arrhythmics include quinidine and procainamide.

  • These drugs can result in QT prolongation in ECG.

questions.stemHtml: The following table gives the data of AUC of drug A alone and AUC of drug A when combined with drug B. p value is <0.01. Which of the following statement regarding these drugs is most correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Drug B decreases the first pass metabolism of drug A

options.label: B
options.text: Drug B increases the systemic metabolism of drug A

options.label: C
options.text: Drug B decreases the intestinal absorption of drug A

options.label: D
options.text: Drug B increases the renal clearance of drug A

questions.answerText: Drug B decreases the first pass metabolism of drug A
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans A) Drug B decreases the first pass metabolism of drug A

 

  • To interpret the data and determine the correct statement, we need to consider the impact of drug B on the pharmacokinetics of drug A.
  • Comparing the AUC values, we can observe that the AUC of drug A is higher when it is combined with drug B compared to when taken alone. This increase in AUC suggests that drug B is affecting the pharmacokinetics of drug A, potentially by altering its metabolism, absorption, or clearance.
  • Now, let's analyze the statements:
    • Drug B decreases the first-pass metabolism of drug A: This statement is the most correct interpretation based on the given data. The increase in AUC of drug A when combined with drug B suggests that drug B is likely inhibiting the first-pass metabolism of drug A. By decreasing first-pass metabolism, more of drug A is able to reach systemic circulation, resulting in a higher AUC.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Drug B increases the systemic metabolism of drug A: This statement is unlikely to be correct because an increase in systemic metabolism would typically result in a lower AUC, not an increase.

 

Option C. Drug B decreases the intestinal absorption of drug A: This statement is unlikely to be correct because a decrease in intestinal absorption would generally result in a lower AUC, not an increase.

 

Option D. Drug B increases the renal clearance of drug A: This statement is unlikely to be correct because an increase in renal clearance would typically result in a lower AUC, not an increase.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy presents to the emergency room with agitation, mydriasis, and hot, dry skin. Physical examination reveals decreased bowel sounds and tachycardia. Assuming that he is suffering from a drug overdose, which class of drugs is most likely responsible for his symptoms?

The symptoms of anticholinergic poisoning (Atropine/Dhatura/Belladona) are:

 

D:      Delirium, Dry Skin

R:      Retention

questions.stem: A drug effect that is produced by therapeutic doses of both timolol and amiodarone is blockade of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Beta-adrenoceptors.

  • Both timolol and amiodarone are medications that have a blocking effect on beta-adrenoceptors. Amiodarone is a non-competitive beta blocker whereas drugs ending with lol (like nadolol) are competitive beta blockers.
  • Timolol is a non-selective beta blocker that blocks both beta-1 and beta-2 adrenoceptors.
  • Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication that has actions of all classes of anti-arrhythmic drugs. It is a blocker of Na channels; K channels and Ca channels and it also has non-selective beta-blocking properties.

questions.stem: Mechanism of action of statins is:

options.label: C
options.text: Indirect increase of LDL receptors synthesis

questions.answerText: Indirect increase of LDL receptors synthesis
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Indirect increase of LDL receptor synthesis

 

  • The mechanism of action of statins involves inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol in the liver. By inhibiting this enzyme, statins reduce the production of cholesterol in the liver. This leads to indirect increase in the synthesis of LDL receptors in the liver, leading to increased uptake and clearance of LDL cholesterol from the bloodstream. This is the primary mechanism by which statins lower LDL cholesterol levels.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Inhibition of HMG-CoA synthase: This is a wrong option as the correct mechanism of action of statins is the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, and not HMG-CoA synthase.

 

Option B. Stimulation of HMG-CoA reductase: This is a wrong option as the correct mechanism of action of statins is the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, not the stimulation.

 

Option D. Inhibition of intestinal cholesterol absorption: This is the major mechanism of action of ezetimibe and statins has negligible action in this regard.

questions.stem: One of the health benefits of the use of combined oral contraceptives in pre-menopausal women is that these contraceptives reduce the risk of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Ovarian cancer

  • Multiple studies have shown that the use of combined oral contraceptives is associated with a decreased risk of developing ovarian cancer. The longer the duration of use, the greater the reduction in risk. This protective effect persists for many years after discontinuing the use of oral contraceptives.
  • The other options listed are not specifically associated with a reduced risk using combined oral contraceptives:
  1. Deep vein thrombosis: Combined oral contraceptives can slightly increase the risk of deep vein thrombosis.
  2. Migraine: The use of combined oral contraceptives may trigger or worsen migraine in some females.
     

Ischemic stroke: The use of combined oral contraceptives can slightly increase the risk of ischemic stroke, particularly in women who have other risk factors such as smoking or hypertension.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of osteoporosis is being evaluated for potential pharmacological treatments to strengthen her bones. She has tried lifestyle modifications, including weight-bearing exercises and calcium supplements, with limited improvement. Her physician is considering various pharmacological agents to inhibit osteoclastic activity and thereby prevent further bone loss. Which of the following medications does NOT primarily act by inhibiting osteoclasts?
questions.solutionHtml:
erif">Ans. C. Teriparatide

 

Explanation of Options:

 

a) Denosumab: This is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the RANKL (Receptor Activator for Nuclear Factor κ B Ligand), which is essential for the formation and function of osteoclasts. Thus, it inhibits osteoclast activity.

 

b) Strontium ranelate: This drug is used in the treatment of osteoporosis and works by both promoting bone formation and inhibiting bone resorption. It is thought to inhibit osteoclasts, although the exact mechanism is not well understood.

 

c) Teriparatide: This is the correct answer. Teriparatide is a recombinant form of parathyroid hormone. It is actually an anabolic (bone-building) agent that stimulates osteoblast activity, rather than inhibiting osteoclasts.

 

d) Raloxifene: This is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that inhibits bone resorption by osteoclasts, thus serving to preserve bone mass in conditions like osteoporosis.

 

Teriparatide does not inhibit osteoclasts but stimulates osteoblasts, making it the correct answer for the drug that does not act by inhibiting osteoclasts.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old male with a history of bipolar disorder presents to the clinic with complaints of confusion, agitation, diarrhea, hand tremors, and excessive thirst. The patient reports taking lithium for the past year as part of his treatment plan. Recently, he also started taking hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension. On examination, the patient has a fine tremor in both hands and is noted to have a serum lithium level of 2.8 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the patient's elevated serum lithium level?

options.label: A
options.text: Additive diuretic effect of hydrochlorothiazide and lithium.

options.label: B
options.text: Increased renal reabsorption of lithium due to hydrochlorothiazide.

options.label: C
options.text: Decreased gastrointestinal absorption of lithium due to hydrochlorothiazide.

questions.answerText: Increased renal reabsorption of lithium due to hydrochlorothiazide.
questions.solutionHtml:
m due to hydrochlorothiazide.

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Additive diuretic effect of hydrochlorothiazide and lithium: While both hydrochlorothiazide and lithium can have diuretic effects, this option doesn't directly explain the elevated serum lithium level. The primary concern here is the elevated lithium level, not an additive diuretic effect.

 

B) Increased renal reabsorption of lithium due to hydrochlorothiazide: Hydrochlorothiazide can increase the renal reabsorption of lithium, leading to elevated serum lithium levels and symptoms of toxicity. This is the most likely explanation for the patient's elevated lithium level.

 

C) Decreased gastrointestinal absorption of lithium due to hydrochlorothiazide: This option is misleading because decreased gastrointestinal absorption of lithium would lead to lower serum lithium levels, not higher.

 

D) Hydrochlorothiazide-induced enhancement of lithium metabolism: This is also a distractor. Enhancement of lithium metabolism would typically result in reduced serum lithium levels, not elevated levels.

 

Therefore, the most likely cause for the elevated serum lithium level and symptoms in this patient is the increased renal reabsorption of lithium due to hydrochlorothiazide.



ore, the most likely cause for the elevated serum lithium level and symptoms in this patient is the increased renal reabsorption of lithium due to hydrochlorothiazide.

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old male with a history of epilepsy presents to the dentist with complaints of difficulty in eating and cleaning the teeth. On Examination, the findings were shown as seen in the diagram below. The patient reports that he has been taking an anti-epileptic drug for the past six months, and his symptoms began to appear gradually over the past few weeks. Which of the following anti-epileptic drugs is likely to produce these adverse effects?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Phenytoin.

 

The patient's symptoms are consistent with gum hypertrophy caused by phenytoin. It can lead to dental problems such as difficulty in eating and cleaning the teeth.

 

Important drugs causing gum hypertrophy are:

 

  • Phenytoin
  • Cyclosporine
  • Calcium channel blockers
     

Carbamazepine is an anti-epileptic drug that can cause ataxia and dizziness, but it does not commonly cause gingival hyperplasia. Gabapentin and levetiracetam are other anti-epileptic drugs that do not typically cause nystagmus, ataxia, or gingival hyperplasia. Therefore, the correct answer is D. Phenytoin.



ore, the correct answer is D. Phenytoin.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old male patient with a history of heart failure and atrial fibrillation has been taking digoxin for several months. He recently started on a new medication for hypertension. He presents to the clinic with symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and visual disturbances. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for these symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
ng="EN-US" style="font-size:12.0pt">Ans. D. Hydrochlorothiazide

 

Explanation:

  • Symptoms of digoxin toxicity include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, and visual disturbances. Other symptoms can include dizziness, confusion, and changes in heart rate or rhythm. Hydrochlorothiazide can cause electrolyte abnormalities such as hypokalemia, which can increase the risk of digoxin toxicity.
  • Metformin is an oral antidiabetic medication that does not interact with digoxin.
  • Lisinopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker, both of which do not interact with digoxin.

questions.stemHtml: Given image shows the Log DRC of a drug alone (A) and in the presence of antagonists (B and C). Identify the type of antagonism shown in curve B and curve C?

options.label: A
options.text: B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist

options.label: B
options.text: B is non-competitive an C is competitive antagonist

questions.answerText: B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist
questions.solutionHtml:
a non-competitive antagonist.

 

Explanation of options:

 

A. B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist: This is the correct answer. B shows a parallel shift to the right, which is characteristic of competitive antagonism. Increasing the concentration of the agonist can overcome the antagonist. C shows a reduction in the maximal response that the agonist can produce, characteristic of a non-competitive antagonist.

 

B. B is non-competitive and C is competitive antagonist: This is incorrect. B shows a parallel shift to the right, which is indicative of competitive antagonism. C shows a reduction in the maximal response, which is indicative of non-competitive antagonism.

 

C. Both are competitive antagonists: This is incorrect. Curve B shows characteristics of competitive antagonism, but curve C shows characteristics of non-competitive antagonism as it reduces the maximal response of the agonist.

 

D. Both are non-competitive antagonists: This is incorrect. Curve B shows characteristics of competitive antagonism as it shifts parallel to the right, while curve C shows characteristics of non-competitive antagonism as it reduces the maximal response of the agonist.

questions.stem: A young female presented with left sided severe throbbing headache associated with nausea, vomiting, photophobia and phonophobia. Which of the following is a new drug that can provide immediate relief to this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Lasmiditan

  • The symptoms described, including severe throbbing headache, nausea, vomiting, photophobia (sensitivity to light), and phonophobia (sensitivity to sound), are characteristic of a migraine headache.
  • Lasmiditan is a new drug that belongs to a class called 5HT1F agonist. It is specifically approved for the acute treatment of migraine attacks in adults. It provides immediate relief by inhibiting the release of CGRP from the neurons.
  • Other drugs mentioned in the options i.e. Propranolol (choice a), Topiramate (choice c) and  Erenumab (choice d) are used for prophylaxis of migraine and not for treatment of acute attack.
  • Propranolol is DOC for prophylaxis of migraine.

questions.stemHtml: Relative intensities of blocking effect (shown by symbol of +) of four drugs on different receptors is: Which drug is most likely to exacerbate the symptoms of Parkinsonism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Drug D

 

  • Parkinson's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by a deficiency of dopamine, which leads to motor symptoms like bradykinesia, tremors, rigidity, and postural instability. The disease affects the dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra of the brain, which normally send signals to the striatum to regulate movements. With the loss of these neurons, the balance between the excitatory (cholinergic) and inhibitory (dopaminergic) signals is disrupted, leading to the motor symptoms.
  • Drugs with high D2 receptor blocking effects would potentially exacerbate the symptoms of Parkinsonism as they would further decrease dopamine activity. Hence, looking at the table, Drug A and Drug D have significant D2 receptor blocking effects (+++). However, Drug A also has muscarinic receptor blocking effects which might reduce the symptoms of Parkinson's (as muscarinic blocking can reduce the overactivity of the cholinergic system).
  • Considering all these factors, the most likely drug to exacerbate the symptoms of Parkinsonism among the options provided would be Drug D.

questions.stem: Which of the following chelating agents can be used orally for the treatment of transfusion siderosis in thalassemia patients?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Deferipirone.

  • Deferipirone is an oral chelating agent that can be used for the treatment of transfusion siderosis in thalassemia patients. Transfusion siderosis refers to the accumulation of excess iron in the body due to frequent blood transfusions, which are often necessary for thalassemia patients.
  • Ferrioxamine is an iron containing compound. When we remove iron from this, the compound formed is called Desferrioxamine which has high affinity for iron.
  • Desferrioxamine (option A) is a chelating agent, but it is administered intravenously or through subcutaneous infusion. Desferrioxamine is commonly used for iron chelation therapy in thalassemia patients, but it is not administered orally.
